qa.question: Within what range do you think GenUI's autonomous decision-making power should be limited?
options: A. Can only execute operations I explicitly specify.
B. Can optimize the execution method but cannot change the goal.
C. Can make autonomous decisions within the boundaries I set.
D. Can be completely autonomous within the domain I authorize.
qa.answer: C - I want to stay in control and set the boundaries myself, but within those limits it's fine if the system makes its own calls since I don't wanna micromanage every little thing.

qa.question: Do you prefer one-time generation or iterative generation? Why?
qa.answer: I definitely prefer iterative generation because I like being able to tweak things and stay in control of what's happening. If the AI just gives me one final result and I can't do anything about it, that's super frustrating — like what if it's not what I wanted? I'd rather go back and forth, adjust stuff, and explore different directions until I get exactly what I need. It feels more like a conversation where I'm still the one calling the shots.

qa.question: When GenUI automatically generates an interface layout, do you want the system to explain the reason for generating that layout?
options: A. Yes; I want a detailed explanation for every generation.
B. Yes; but only when the result does not match expectations.
C. Not necessarily; only when the explanation is useful.
D. No; as long as the result is useful, I don't need an explanation.
qa.answer: B - I want to know why it did something weird because if it's not what I expected, I need to understand what went wrong so I can fix it or tell it what I actually want.

qa.question: How do you view the identity transparency issue when an AI simulates an "Expert Tone" to answer questions?
qa.answer: Honestly, it kinda bugs me when an AI talks like it's some expert professor and you can't even tell if it's actually pulling from legit sources or just making stuff sound convincing. Like, I want to explore data and learn things, but I also want to know when I'm talking to a machine versus getting actual expert-backed info. It feels like a control thing for me — if the AI is faking confidence, I lose my ability to judge what's real and what's not. They should at least be upfront about it instead of trying to sound all authoritative when it might just be hallucinating or whatever.

qa.question: Through which way do you prefer to understand the overall structure of a GenUI-generated interface?
options: A. Viewing an interface map or navigation tree.
B. Exploring page by page.
C. Summarizing rules after completing specific tasks.
D. Reading product documentation or instructions.
qa.answer: A - I'd rather just see a map or tree of the whole thing upfront so I know where everything is without having to click around and waste time.

qa.question: When processing cross-linguistic information, what is your standard for understanding AI translation accuracy?
qa.answer: Honestly, I don't have like a super technical standard for judging translation accuracy. I'm a native Spanish speaker so when something gets translated between Spanish and English, I can usually tell right away if it sounds off or if the meaning got twisted. My basic standard is just—does it sound natural and does it actually say what was meant? If I read a translation and it feels robotic or misses the tone of what someone was trying to say, that's when I know it's not accurate enough. I get kind of anxious when I have to rely on AI for translations in languages I don't know because I have no way to verify it myself.

qa.question: When the system provides historical records or traceability, you will:
options: A. Become more reliant.
B. Slightly increase reliance.
C. Feel no significant change.
D. Not care.
qa.answer: B - Having a record of what happened before makes me feel a little more comfortable using it again, but I still don't fully trust these systems enough to rely on them heavily.

qa.question: Are you willing to let GenUI complete complex tasks for you? Why?
qa.answer: Honestly, I'm kind of torn on that. Part of me is curious to see what it can do, and if it saves me time on boring stuff while I'm juggling multiple projects, that's a win. But I also get nervous about trusting it with something complex because what if it messes up and I don't even understand what went wrong? I'd probably let it handle simpler parts of a bigger task, but I'd want really clear feedback on what it's doing so I'm not left in the dark.

qa.question: When facing an extra-long response generated by AI, your first psychological reaction is:
options: A. Excitement; I feel it's full of information and worth digging into.
B. Anxiety; I feel reading pressure and wish for a short summary.
C. Fatigue; I skip it directly and ask the AI to "get to the point."
qa.answer: B - I immediately feel overwhelmed and stressed because I just want the answer quickly without having to wade through a wall of text.

qa.question: When using GenUI, do you increase decision-making time because of the fear that an "operation is irreversible"? Please describe the impact of this psychology on your efficiency.
qa.answer: Yeah, honestly this happens to me a lot. Like if I'm not sure whether I can undo something, I'll just sit there staring at the screen way longer than I should, second-guessing myself. It really kills my productivity because I'm already trying to juggle multiple things at once, and that hesitation just adds up. I wish these tools would just clearly tell me "hey, you can undo this" so I don't have to stress about it. When things feel permanent and there's no clear way back, I'd rather not click anything at all, which kind of defeats the whole purpose of using the tool.

qa.question: When you need to modify a detail, you:
options: A. Change the interface directly.
B. Re-describe the requirement.
C. Try multiple times.
D. Give up on the modification.
qa.answer: B - I'd rather just explain what I need differently since I'm not super comfortable messing with interface settings directly.

qa.question: When the content generated by AI requires high-frequency correction from you, how long do you usually persist before choosing to completely give up on collaboration?
qa.answer: Honestly, not very long. If I have to correct it more than like three or four times and it's still not getting what I need, I start feeling really frustrated and anxious about wasting my time. I'd say maybe five to ten minutes max before I just close the thing and try to do it myself or find another way. I'm usually juggling other stuff anyway, so I don't have the patience to babysit an AI that keeps getting it wrong.

qa.question: If the AI's tone becomes very aggressive or strange, you would first:
options: A. Think its logic collapsed due to context interference.
B. Suspect that the safety filter behind it has failed.
C. Think it is simulating a specific personality trait.
qa.answer: B - That would freak me out honestly, and my first thought would be that something broke in whatever safety system is supposed to keep it from acting like that.

qa.question: Describe the level of transparency you want GenUI to maintain regarding user data usage and how this affects your willingness to use it.
qa.answer: Honestly, I get pretty anxious about where my data goes, so I need these tools to be upfront about what they're collecting and why. I don't want to dig through pages of legal jargon to figure it out — just tell me clearly what's happening with my info. If something feels shady or unclear, I'll just stop using it because the stress isn't worth it. I'm already not using these tools that often, so it wouldn't take much for me to walk away if I don't trust how they handle my data.

qa.question: If GenUI generates an interaction pattern you have never seen before, you will:
options: A. Try to operate based on my own intuition.
B. Look for guided prompts or tutorials.
C. Give up using the function.
D. Contact support or consult documentation.
qa.answer: B - I want to know exactly what something does before I press it, so I'd look for some kind of guide or prompt to tell me clearly what to do.

qa.question: When using GenUI, how do you distinguish between "functions customized for me by AI" and "system-default functions"?
qa.answer: Honestly, it's not always easy to tell the difference, and that bothers me. I want to know exactly what the system decided on its own versus what it's doing because it thinks it knows what I want. If something looks different from what I'm used to or shows up unexpectedly, I get suspicious and uncomfortable — I didn't ask for that change. I wish they would just label things clearly, like put a little mark or different color on anything the AI changed, so I'm not left guessing and feeling like I've lost control of my own screen.

qa.question: When the AI cannot answer a question and proactively admits "I don't know," your trust in it:
options: A. Increases; I find it honest and aware of its boundaries.
B. Decreases; I feel its capability is limited and it isn't "smart" enough.
C. No feeling; it's just a standard programmed response.
qa.answer: A - I find it honest and aware of its boundaries.

qa.question: When using GenUI, do you intentionally reserve certain tasks to be completed independently by yourself? Please explain your selection logic.
qa.answer: Yes, absolutely. I don't let the system handle anything where I need to feel certain about the outcome — like final decisions on layout choices or anything involving my personal preferences. I've been around long enough to know that if you hand over too much control, you end up with something that doesn't feel like yours anymore. I'll use it for the tedious parts, like generating options or doing repetitive adjustments, but the final say is always mine. If I can't clearly see what it's doing and why, I'd rather just do it myself.

qa.question: When the interface requires frequent confirmation of operations, you:
options: A. Accept the confirmation.
B. Feel slightly annoyed.
C. Skip the confirmation.
D. Become impatient.
qa.answer: A - I actually prefer having confirmations because it gives me a sense of control and reassurance that I'm not accidentally doing something I didn't intend.

qa.question: Talk about your cognitive experience with "auto-paging" or "infinite scroll" dialogue flows.
qa.answer: I find infinite scroll quite frustrating, to be honest. On my phone, I lose track of where I was, and there's no clear sense of how much is left or where things begin and end. I prefer pages with clear boundaries — I want to feel like I'm in control of moving forward, not being dragged along by the system. It makes me anxious when content just keeps loading without any indication of progress or a stopping point.

qa.question: When you and the AI disagree, your final decision logic is:
options: A. Always insist on my own view; the AI is just a reference.
B. Try to persuade the AI and see if its counter-arguments can move me.
C. Listen to the AI in most cases because it has seen more data.
qa.answer: A - I always go with my own judgment because I need to feel in control, and the AI is just a tool that should follow what I want, not the other way around.

qa.question: How do you use rollback or history functions to optimize operations?
qa.answer: I use the undo button quite a lot, actually. When the system changes something I didn't ask for or moves things around without my permission, I need to go back to where I was before. I don't like having to dig through complicated history panels though — I just want a simple way to step back one or two actions. If I can't easily undo what happened, I get quite frustrated and sometimes I just close the whole thing and start over, which wastes my time.

qa.question: If the AI could show its model's "Attention Weights" through visual charts, you would:
options: A. View them frequently to help me optimize the weight distribution of my prompts.
B. Occasionally try to take a look, but give up because it's too professional.
C. Think this is for technical staff; it is meaningless to me.
qa.answer: C - I don't need to see technical charts and numbers; I just want the tool to do what I tell it to do clearly and simply.

qa.question: How do you view the transparency of the system?
qa.answer: I find it quite frustrating when the system does things without explaining why or how it arrived at a particular result. I need to see clearly what's happening at each step — if it just changes something on its own without telling me, I feel uneasy and out of control. At my age, I don't have patience for guessing games. I want straightforward feedback, not some mysterious process happening behind the scenes that I can't follow or undo.

qa.question: How do you distinguish between "Dialogue Mode" and "Creation Mode"?
options: A. Can clearly distinguish the difference in thinking logic between the two.
B. Think there is no difference; both involve typing in a chat box.
C. Rely on visual cues in the interface (e.g., colors, icons) to distinguish.
qa.answer: C - I usually just look at how the screen looks different, like if there are different colors or icons, because I don't really think about the logic behind it that much.

qa.question: How do you view the "next step" suggestions the AI automatically generates for you?
qa.answer: Honestly, I find them kind of helpful when they actually match what I'm trying to do, like if I'm working on a school project and it suggests something relevant. But a lot of the time they feel random or pushy, like the AI is trying to decide for me what I should do next, and that really bothers me. I'd rather just have the option to ask for suggestions when I want them instead of having them pop up automatically. I like being in control of my own workflow, even if I'm not super techy about it.

qa.question: When the system provides auto-fill or automated operations, you will:
options: A. Accept all of them.
B. Accept them after checking.
C. Accept them partially.
D. Not use them.
qa.answer: B - I'd want to check everything first because I like being in control of what goes into my work, even if the auto-fill saves me time.

qa.question: How do you view system uncertainty?
qa.answer: Honestly, it kind of stresses me out when the system isn't sure about something because I just want it to give me a clear answer so I can get my work done. Like if it's uncertain, I'd rather it just tells me straight up instead of giving me something that might be wrong without warning me. I guess I'd want it to be upfront about it so I can decide what to do myself, because I really don't like feeling like I'm not in control of what's happening. It makes me a bit anxious when I can't tell if the output is reliable or not.

qa.question: If GenUI automatically creates a complex Kanban board for you, your first choice is to:
options: A. Immediately adjust the layout to fit my habits.
B. Run it once following the AI's logic without changing things easily.
C. Choose to close it directly because I don't understand how to use it.
qa.answer: A - I'd want to fix it up right away so it works the way I like, because I don't really feel comfortable using something that's set up in a way I didn't choose.

qa.question: After using GenUI continuously for a long time, how do you usually recover your attention and reduce fatigue?
qa.answer: Honestly, I usually just close my laptop and take a break from screens altogether. I might lie on my bed and scroll through my phone for a bit or listen to music to kind of reset my brain. Sometimes I'll get a snack or make some tea because it gives me something simple to do that doesn't require thinking. I don't really have a fancy routine or anything, I just need to step away for a while before I can focus again.

qa.question: When the system predicts your next step, you:
options: A. Accept the prediction.
B. Accept after checking.
C. Modify the prediction.
D. Ignore the prediction.
qa.answer: B - I usually accept it after checking because I want to make sure it's actually doing what I need it to do before I let it go ahead.

qa.question: In what situations do you want complete control over the interface?
qa.answer: Honestly, I want complete control pretty much all the time when I'm working on my content stuff. Like if I'm making something for a school project or editing a post, I don't want the AI randomly changing where things are or suggesting layouts I didn't ask for. It stresses me out when things move around without me doing it because then I have to figure out how to get it back to what I wanted. I just want it to do what I tell it to do and stay put until I decide to change something myself.

qa.question: In what form do you think GenUI's explanation information should be presented most appropriately?
options: A. Short text description (one-sentence summary).
B. Detailed step-by-step description (itemized explanation).
C. Visual charts (e.g., decision path diagrams).
D. Interactive explanation (expand details on demand).
qa.answer: D - I like being able to control how much info I see, so having the option to expand details only when I want them feels less overwhelming and lets me focus on my work.

qa.question: Do you want the system to provide traceable operation records? Why?
qa.answer: Yes, I really want that. Like, when I'm working on my content and the system changes something or generates something, I want to be able to see exactly what it did and when. It makes me feel more in control because sometimes I don't fully understand what's happening behind the scenes, and having a record means I can go back and undo stuff if I need to. I get kind of anxious when things change without me knowing why, so having that history would make me feel way more comfortable using it.

qa.question: When you first see an AI-generated interface (GenUI), what do you usually do?
options: A. Start using it immediately, figure it out as I go.
B. Browse the overall layout first before starting any operations.
C. Look for help documents or instructions before using it.
D. Compare the interface style with my expectations before deciding how to proceed.
qa.answer: A - I just dive right in and start clicking around because that's the fastest way to figure out what it can do.

qa.question: Please describe the process of building operational confidence in a completely unfamiliar GenUI environment.
qa.answer: Honestly, I'd just start tapping around and seeing what happens — like I'm not gonna read a manual or whatever. If the system gives me clear feedback when I do something, like visual cues or confirmations, I build confidence pretty fast because I can tell what's actually working. But if I click something and nothing happens or I get some vague response, that's when I get frustrated and start losing trust in the whole thing. I need the UI to basically react to me in real-time so I can figure out the boundaries of what it can do, and then I'll push those boundaries on purpose to see how far I can go.

qa.question: When the interface provides recommended operations, you:
options: A. Always execute according to the recommendation.
B. Accept them in most cases.
C. Accept them only when they seem reasonable.
D. Basically ignore the recommendations.
qa.answer: C - I only go with recommendations if they actually make sense to me because I like being in control of what happens and I don't trust the system blindly.

qa.question: When you feel uncertain while using GenUI, are you more inclined to "trust the AI to proceed" or "pause and seek confirmation"? What factors influence your choice?
qa.answer: Honestly, I'm way more inclined to pause and seek confirmation because I HATE when things go in a direction I didn't want and then I have no idea how to undo it. Like if the AI isn't giving me clear feedback about what it's about to do, I'm not just gonna let it run wild with my code or whatever. But if I'm just exploring something low-stakes out of curiosity, like generating a quick UI mockup or something, I'll let it do its thing because worst case I just start over. The biggest factor is honestly whether I feel like I'm in control—if the system makes it easy to undo or shows me exactly what's happening, I'll trust it more, but vague outputs with no explanation? Nah, I'm hitting pause immediately.

qa.question: When the system provides shortcuts, you:
options: A. Use them proactively.
B. Use them occasionally.
C. Rarely use them.
D. Do not use them.
qa.answer: A - I love shortcuts because they let me get things done faster and I like feeling in control of the flow instead of waiting around.

qa.question: When the interface is inconsistent, how do you adapt?
qa.answer: Honestly it's so annoying when things are inconsistent because I just want to figure stuff out quickly, especially when I'm on my phone between classes or whatever. I usually just tap around aggressively until I find what I'm looking for — like trial and error but faster because I trust my gut. If something keeps being weird and I can't get clear feedback on what's happening, I'll get frustrated pretty fast and might just close the app entirely. I'd rather find a different tool than waste my time guessing what the UI wants from me.

qa.question: When you can guide the GenUI generation step-by-step, you:
options: A. Input requirements all at once.
B. Adjust in steps.
C. Modify frequently.
D. Are unsure how to guide it.
qa.answer: B - I like adjusting in steps because it gives me more control over what's happening and I can actually see how each change affects the output.

qa.question: When the collaboration plan provided by AI is completely beyond your professional cognitive boundary, how do you maintain control?
qa.answer: Honestly, if the AI throws something at me that's totally beyond what I know, I'm not just gonna sit there and accept it blindly—I'd start poking at it, asking it to break things down or explain why it chose that approach. Like, I need to understand the reasoning or I literally cannot trust it. I'd probably also just google stuff on my phone real quick to cross-check whether it's making sense or feeding me garbage. If it still feels off and I can't get clear feedback on what's happening, I'd rather scrap the plan and tell it to try again with something I can actually follow, because what's the point of a "collaboration" if I have zero control over what's going on?

qa.question: When do you think GenUI's transparency information should be presented?
options: A. Proactively displayed before the AI executes the operation.
B. Automatically attached after the AI executes the operation.
C. Displayed only when the user proactively requests it.
D. Automatically popped up at key decision nodes.
qa.answer: A - I want to know what's about to happen before it happens so I can decide if I'm okay with it, because honestly nothing's more annoying than an AI just doing stuff without telling you first.

qa.question: When an explanation given by GenUI conflicts with your intuition, how do you decide which side to believe? Describe your thought process.
qa.answer: Honestly, I usually trust my gut first because if something feels off, there's probably a reason. Like, I'll quickly Google it or check Stack Overflow on my phone to see if other people agree with what the AI is saying, because I've had times where GenUI gives me something that sounds confident but is just... wrong. If I can't find anything to back up either side, I'll just test it myself — like run the code and see what actually happens. I hate when AI explanations are vague or wishy-washy because then I can't even tell if it's conflicting with my intuition or just being unclear, which is so frustrating.

qa.question: When you enter a vague command (e.g., "optimize this"), you expect the AI to:
options: A. Automatically guess my intent and provide the result directly.
B. Stop and ask for specific optimization dimensions (e.g., word count, tone, logic).
C. Provide three different versions of optimization for me to choose from.
qa.answer: B - I need the system to ask me exactly what I mean because I want to stay in control of the outcome and not waste time going back and forth fixing something it guessed wrong.

qa.question: To what extent do you think GenUI should actively explain the reasons for interface changes to users? In what form would you like this explanation to be presented?
qa.answer: Honestly, I think the system should always tell me why something changed on my screen. I don't like when things just shift around without warning — it makes me feel like I'm not in control of what's happening. A short, simple sentence at the top of the screen explaining what changed and why would work fine for me. Keep it structured and straightforward, don't give me some long paragraph or a popup I have to dismiss. I just need to know what happened so I can decide if I'm good with it or if I want to undo it.

qa.question: If the AI makes a mistake on a minor issue, your trust in its ability to handle subsequent complex problems:
options: A. Collapses instantly; I view the entire system as unreliable.
B. Drops slightly; I will check its output more frequently.
C. Is largely unaffected; I consider local errors to be a matter of probability.
qa.answer: B - If it messes up on something small, I'm going to be double-checking what it gives me going forward, especially on anything more complicated.

qa.question: How do you view system uncertainty?
qa.answer: I view system uncertainty as something that needs to be communicated clearly and directly. If the system isn't sure about something, just tell me straight up — don't waste my time letting me think everything is solid when it's not. I appreciate when things are structured and upfront, so I can make my own call on whether to trust the output or not. At the end of the day, I need to feel like I'm in control of the decision, not the machine.

qa.question: If there are too many operation options in the GenUI interface, you usually:
options: A. Evaluate each option one by one before making a decision.
B. Consider only the first few options and choose quickly.
C. Request the AI to reduce the number of options.
D. Operate directly according to the default recommendation.
qa.answer: A - I like to take my time and evaluate what's in front of me before I commit to anything, especially when I'm not that familiar with the tool.

qa.question: Please describe a "smooth and effortless" scenario you experienced in GenUI. What design made you feel at ease?
qa.answer: Honestly, I haven't had too many experiences with these AI design tools since I only use them once in a while when I'm curious about something. But there was one time I was messing around on my phone with a tool that laid everything out in clear sections with big buttons and straightforward options — no clutter, no guessing what to tap next. That felt smooth to me because I didn't have to think too hard about where things were; it just made sense. I appreciate when the interface doesn't try to be too clever and just gives me a structured path to follow without a bunch of loading screens slowing me down.

qa.question: In a creative task, what role do you usually want to play?
options: A. Director: Provide the core creative idea and let the AI handle all detailed execution.
B. Architect: Build the framework, let the AI fill in the materials, and then I perform the final refinements.
C. Editor: Let the AI write the first draft, and then I perform large-scale rewriting and auditing.
qa.answer: B - I like to set up the structure and have control over the framework, then let the tool do some of the filling in, but I want to be the one making the final call on what stays.

qa.question: If an AI's suggestion makes you feel manipulated, what action would you take to regain control?
qa.answer: If I felt like the AI was trying to push me in a direction I didn't choose, I'd shut it down immediately and go back to doing things manually. I'm not the type to let a tool run me — I run the tools. I'd probably dig into whatever settings are available to turn off those kinds of suggestions or limit what it can do on its own. At the end of the day, if I can't trust it to stay in its lane, I'd just stop using it altogether.

qa.question: How do you understand "Auto-adjustment" logic in GenUI?
options: A. I believe the system is monitoring my behavior and performing profile analysis.
B. I believe the system is performing rule matching based on the current task type.
C. I view it as magic; I don't understand the underlying mechanism at all.
qa.answer: A - I believe the system is monitoring my behavior and performing profile analysis.

qa.question: Do you think there is a contradiction between "AI Transparency" and "User Privacy"? How do you hope to balance these in GenUI?
qa.answer: Honestly, I haven't thought too deeply about this from a technical standpoint, but I can see where there could be tension between the two. On one hand, I want to know what the system is doing with my information and why it's making certain choices—that's the transparency piece. On the other hand, I don't want it storing or exposing my personal data just to explain itself. I'd hope these GenUI tools can give me clear, straightforward explanations of how they work without needing to dig into my private details to do it. Keep the layout simple, tell me what's happening, but keep my business my business.

qa.question: When you enter a vague command (e.g., "optimize this"), you expect the AI to:
options: A. Automatically guess my intent and provide the result directly.
B. Stop and ask for specific optimization dimensions (e.g., word count, tone, logic).
C. Provide three different versions of optimization for me to choose from.
qa.answer: B - I need the system to ask me what exactly I mean because "optimize" could mean a hundred different things, and I don't want to waste time undoing something I never asked for.

qa.question: What is your standard for a "good prompt"? Please provide an example you commonly use.
qa.answer: For me, a good prompt is one that's direct and gets me what I need without a bunch of back-and-forth. I don't have time to be crafting elaborate instructions when I'm juggling lesson planning, grading, and trying to have a conversation at the same time. I usually go with something like "Give me three discussion questions for 10th graders on [topic], focus on critical thinking, keep it simple." If the system can't figure out what I mean from a clear, straightforward request like that, then honestly that's a design problem, not a me problem. I shouldn't have to jump through hoops to get a usable output.

qa.question: When GenUI recommends multiple plans for you to choose from, your basis for selection is usually:
options: A. The plans ranked highest by the AI.
B. The plan that best fits my personal preferences.
C. The plan that looks safest and carries the lowest risk.
D. The plan that can complete the task the fastest.
qa.answer: C - I tend to go with whatever feels safest because I don't want to deal with unexpected problems or complications when I'm already juggling multiple things.

qa.question: If the AI shows an obvious bias toward a certain viewpoint, would you try to correct it or stop using it?
qa.answer: I'd probably try to correct it first, because I know how these systems work and I'm not about to just accept whatever it feeds me without pushing back. But honestly, if it keeps pushing the same slant after I've called it out, I'm done—I don't have the patience or the energy to keep fighting a tool that's supposed to be helping me. I'm not looking for something that validates one perspective; I need it to give me straight information so I can form my own conclusions. Life's stressful enough without having to babysit an AI's biases on top of everything else.

qa.question: When the interface supports personalization settings, you:
options: A. Make deep adjustments.
B. Make simple settings.
C. Keep the defaults.
D. Do not use them.
qa.answer: C - I don't really have the patience to mess around with settings when the defaults work well enough and I'd rather just get on with what I'm doing.

qa.question: When you are using GenUI to handle high-pressure or urgent tasks, which system designs help or hinder you from staying focused?
qa.answer: When I'm under pressure, the last thing I need is some overly complex interface throwing a bunch of options at me or rearranging itself without warning. Clear feedback is what keeps me grounded—I need to know immediately whether the system processed my input or if something went wrong, not some vague loading spinner with no context. What really hinders me is when the UI decides to get creative and generate some novel layout I've never seen before right when I'm trying to move fast; that's not helpful, that's disorienting. I work better when the system keeps things predictable and gives me straightforward confirmation at each step so I can stay task-focused without second-guessing what's happening underneath.

qa.question: In which type of task do you think human-AI collaboration can exert the greatest value?
options: A. Analysis tasks that require processing large amounts of data.
B. Design tasks that require a combination of creativity and judgment.
C. Operation tasks that require precise execution and have low fault tolerance.
D. Complex tasks that require integrating information across systems.
qa.answer: A - When I'm juggling multiple things at once, having AI crunch through large amounts of data and surface what matters is where I get the most value without having to wrestle with overly complex interfaces.

qa.question: How do you use rollback or history functions to optimize operations?
qa.answer: I use rollback pretty heavily when I'm multitasking and accidentally go down the wrong path—like if I'm tweaking a workflow and it gets more convoluted instead of simpler, I just revert and start over rather than trying to fix the mess. I don't have the patience to carefully plan every step, so having that safety net means I can move fast and not stress about breaking things. History functions are useful for comparing what I had before versus what changed, especially when the interface decides to rearrange itself and I need to figure out what went wrong. Honestly, if a system doesn't have clear undo/rollback with obvious feedback that it actually worked, I get irritated fast because I'm not about to guess whether my action took effect or not.

qa.question: In what form do you think GenUI's explanation information should be presented most appropriately?
options: A. Short text description (one-sentence summary).
B. Detailed step-by-step description (itemized explanation).
C. Visual charts (e.g., decision path diagrams).
D. Interactive explanation (expand details on demand).
qa.answer: A - I don't need a whole production, just tell me what you did in one clear sentence so I can keep moving with my tasks.

qa.question: Do you want the system to provide traceable operation records? Why?
qa.answer: Yes, I want traceable operation records. If something goes wrong or the system makes a change I didn't ask for, I need to be able to look back and see exactly what happened and when. I don't have time to guess what the system did behind the scenes, especially when I'm juggling multiple tasks at once. Clear records also help me figure out if the AI is actually learning what I need or just making things more complicated.
